papers.body: arXiv:2610.38195v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large-scale crystal databases have transformed materials discovery by making millions of structures and thermodynamic properties accessible to materials informatics. Yet dynamical stability remains sparsely characterized at a comparable scale because its evaluation is substantially more computationally demanding than conventional structure and energy calculations. This mismatch creates a critical gap between the rapidly expanding crystal-structure space and the physical information available for materials research and machine learning. Here we introduce Crystoria, a large-scale crystal dataset designed to bring dynamical stability to the scale

papers.title: Strain-Induced BCC-to-FCC Transformation in Tungsten Uncovered by Molecular Dynamics Simulations with Machine Learning Potentials
papers.body: arXiv:2610.38477v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Polymorphic transformations occur in a minority of metals. Tungsten is not one of them. papers.body: arXiv:2610.38850v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum materials exhibit diverse electronic and functional phenomena, but their characterization requires extensive experimental expertise, iterative decision-making and accumulated laboratory knowledge that is difficult to document and transfer. Here we introduce Quantum Agent (QUANTA), an agentic artificial intelligence (AI) framework for autonomous quantum-materials characterization. papers.body: arXiv:2610.38876v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The continuous development of machine learning inter-atomic potentials (MLIAPs)has greatly accelerated materials research in recent years. However, the need to con- struct custom MLIAPs for each unique problem remains a bottleneck which raises the question of the transferability of MLIAPs. papers.title: Development and application of a machine learning potential for diamond surfaces and their sliding interfaces with silicon nitride and silica: effect of passivation, orientation and load
papers.body: arXiv:2610.38937v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Friction and wear of diamond are controlled by its surface chemistry, which determines whether covalent bonds form across the sliding interface. First-principles simulations have explored the role of surface orientation and passivation, but are limited to a few hundred atoms and tens of picoseconds. papers.title: Interpretable neural equation learning for high-dimensional materials data
papers.body: arXiv:2610.37880v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Equation learning seeks to discover compact, interpretable equations from data using various machine-learning techniques. papers.title: Distilling Large-Scale Machine Learning Interatomic Potentials to Predict Long-Timescale Electrolyte Transport Properties
papers.body: arXiv:2610.39513v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Accurately predicting the transport properties of liquid electrolytes is critical for next-generation battery design and requires force fields that are both quantum-mechanically accurate and fast enough for long-timescale simulation. papers.title: Does System Size Matter in Uncertainty Quantification for Machine Learning Interatomic Potentials?
papers.body: arXiv:2610.40126v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Machine-learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) commonly use uncertainty estimates to flag out-of-distribution (OOD) configurations and select structures for active learning. A key question is whether the resulting structure-level uncertainty scores remain comparable across different system sizes. A common practice is to aggregate per-atom uncertainties by their mean or maximum and compare the resulting score against a fixed threshold, implicitly assuming such comparability. papers.title: Framework-Conditional Open Materials Generation
papers.body: arXiv:2610.40443v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Theoretical predictions of novel materials rely on a variety of techniques, from data-mining-based ion substitution methods to fully de novo generative models. Each approach imposes specific constraints and encounters unique challenges when extrapolating beyond the distribution of known materials to discover new ones. The foremost goal of materials generation is to produce stable, unique, and novel (S.U.N.) structures. papers.title: ML-COHP: predicting bond descriptors using latent space of a universal interatomic potentials
papers.body: arXiv:2610.40445v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The integrated crystal orbital Hamilton population (ICOHP) is the standard measure of bond strength in a DFT calculation, but every structure needs its own DFT single point and LOBSTER projection, which takes days for a cell of a hundred atoms, such as a grain boundary or a catalytic nanoparticle. We predict ICOHP from the frozen descriptors of a MACE foundation model. A symmetric pair head reads the scalar and bond-projected vector channels of the two atoms and corrects a pair baseline built from the element embeddings of the same model. We tested the model on the high-entropy diboride (Hf,Zr,Ti,Nb,Ta)B$_2$, Pt clusters on defective graphene

papers.body: arXiv:2510.23064v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) bridge the gap between quantum-mechanical accuracy and scalable molecular simulations. papers.body: arXiv:2608.21525v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The application of density functional theory to heterogeneous catalysis is hindered by the shortcomings of conventional density functional approximations. We combine machine learning with explicitly non-local physically informed descriptors and introduce an exchange-correlation functional (CIDER26SS) framework regularized for wide transferability. CIDER26SS is size-extensive, highly efficient, provides a balanced and accurate description of both molecular and solid-state systems, and is specifically well-optimized for transition metal surface chemistry.
